title: Understanding and Enabling Score Distillation in Continuous Diffusion Language Models

summary.en: NIPSD adapts score-based distribution matching to continuous diffusion language models through teacher-trajectory warmup, noise-interpolated perturbations, and continuous student-score estimation. It enables one-step and few-step generation with FLM and LangFlow while resolving token uncertainty and preserving variation across samples.
summary.zh: NIPSD 通过教师轨迹预热、噪声插值扰动和连续学生 score 估计，将基于 score 的分布匹配迁移到连续扩散语言模型，在降低 token 不确定性的同时保留样本间变化，实现 FLM 与 LangFlow 的一步及少步生成。

cover.alt: Animated conceptual overview of NIPSD: a frozen CDLM teacher guides distillation through CD warmup, noise-interpolated perturbations, and FiTScore; at inference, only the distilled generator maps noise to joint token outputs in one or a few evaluations.

note.en: Table 2: one-step NIPSD models are initialized from already-distilled two-step generators and trained with Diff-Instruct (DI). GenPPL is evaluated by GPT-2 Large on 1,024 generated samples; entropy is mean per-sample unigram entropy. These scores do not measure wall-clock speedup.
